attempts.prompt: Edit this exact existing original-project WARP bay background into its EMPTY MODULAR BAY state. This is a precise local equipment removal, not a redesign. Preserve the source's same wide landscape composition, frontal camera, vanishing point, scale, architecture, upper side galleries/railings, dark green-black ribbed walls, ceiling machinery/ring light, cables integrated into walls, attached wall trophy reliefs, dark red cloth banners, worn bronze/black metal textures, turquoise ceiling illumination, restrained red architectural strips, atmospheric depth, and large foreground floor panels with the front rim/steps. REMOVE ONLY THE PAINTED-IN MODULAR EQUIPMENT that must be supplied separately in the game: both enormous freestanding blade-shaped warp portal pylons at left/right of the central floor (including their bases, attached projecting braces and dedicated portal hoses), both freestanding red-screen control consoles at far left and right on the lower floor, and the dedicated round raised warp-portal platform between the two pylons, including its red ring and attached front little control lip. Replace the exposed portions by a faithful seamless continuation of the source's EXISTING room back wall and EXISTING broad flat metal floor panel pattern. The floor must be one unobstructed empty playable band across the entire room, with clear space reserved for future separate portal, coordinate console, reactor and return beacon props. Do not leave ghost pylons, console shadows, floating device interfaces, painted gateway, glowing portal membrane, portal ring on the floor or new equipment. Preserve architectural side-wall buttresses that are part of the room; only detachable modular portal equipment goes away. No people, creatures, labels, text captions, new furniture, new doorway or changed camera. Keep the original aspect/layout and material palette faithfully. This image is a complete intentionally OPAQUE BACKGROUND, filling all pixels; do not produce a cutout or transparent holes. Native opaque PNG. No claim of official canon certification or human approval.
